text: Before I let you all go to the keynote, I have three more tips just to recap what we talked about, things that you should keep in mind if you're using the app server.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The first one is you should actually ship your own version of the harness.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: This will eliminate so many headaches for you.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: If you're relying on the user's installed CLI, you're going to constantly run into things from breaking changes, even though we are trying to minimize them.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: But if you're relying on experimental features, that might happen.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: But you also don't have to worry about whether a user has actually updated their version and has the latest feature that you want to use or have them nudge them updating it.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So ship your own version of the harness.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The other part is you should absolutely expose new functions as part of your interface.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We do this with the Codex app, for example, for it to be able to control itself as part of the Codex thread, like spinning up automations, et cetera.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: But mark them as deferred.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: That way you're not polluting the context window unnecessarily with all of the different additional functions that you're adding, and instead still have them available for the agent without necessarily confusing it.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And if you are changing the instructions, try to start with adding developer instructions rather than changing the base instructions.
